subject: Insurance
title: The Great Chicago Fire
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Great Chicago Fire.

hook.text: On October 8, 1871, Chicago burned for two days. 17,500 buildings destroyed, 100,000 homeless.

buildup.text: Chicago was built of wood. The fire spread so fast that firefighters couldn't even reach the worst areas in time.

discovery.text: Insurance claims totaled $200 million (about $5 billion today). Only $88 million was actually paid.

twist.text: The bankruptcies taught insurers a brutal lesson: never concentrate too much risk in one city.

climax.text: Chicago's fire destroyed the old insurance model.

quiz.question: What lesson did insurers learn from the Chicago fire?
